short: The Colossus of Rhodes was a massive bronze statue of the sun god Helios and one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
full:
Erected between 292 and 280 BCE to celebrate the island's successful defence against a year-long siege, the Colossus of Rhodes was a monumental achievement of Hellenistic engineering. Designed by the sculptor Chares of Lindos, the statue stood approximately 33 metres high, making it the tallest statue of the ancient world.

Constructed from bronze plates over an iron and stone framework, it stood near the harbour entrance, though likely not straddling it as later legends claimed. The Colossus stood for only 54 years before snapping at the knees and toppling during a devastating earthquake in 226 BCE. The massive ruins lay on the ground for centuries, continuing to attract travellers and admirers until they were finally sold for scrap in the 7th century CE.
